name: Golden Visa (Long-Term Residence)

requirements.blocker_text: Wholly-owned property valued at a minimum of AED 2,000,000 (loans permitted only from locally-approved banks).
Requires comprehensive health insurance for the investor and family members.
Owns an active SME generating at least AED 1,000,000 in annual revenue.
Founder of a previous venture (or ventures) sold for a total value of at least AED 7,000,000.
Holds approval from a recognized UAE business incubator.

AED 2,000,000 deposited in an investment fund or national bank, OR an enterprise established with AED 2,000,000 capital, OR a partnership stake worth AED 2,000,000+; alternatively, ownership of a business paying AED 250,000+ in annual federal tax, or a partnership share equivalent to that tax contribution.

Recognized exceptional talent in culture, innovation, sports, AI/blockchain and other key sectors, science, specialized professions, or as a top graduate or humanitarian worker -- assessed on a discretionary, merit basis rather than a fixed numeric threshold.

evidence_required.document: Supporting evidence per category (title deed, financial statements, sale agreements, incubator letter, awards/recommendation letters)

outcome.duration_length: long-term, renewed every 10 years depending on category and continued eligibility

sources.title: Ministry of Economy and Tourism, Government of the UAE -- Investment FAQs: Golden Visa routes -- real estate (AED 2M), business/entrepreneurship (SME AED 1M revenue, or prior exit AED 7M, or incubator approval), public investment (AED 2M deposit/capital/partnership or AED 250k annual tax), and talent categories (culture, innovation, sports, AI/blockchain, science, top graduates, humanitarian workers); renewed every 10 years

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the UAE's full build-out. leads_to_citizenship modelled as false: the UAE has no pathway to citizenship from ordinary or long-term residence of any kind, including the Golden Visa -- confirmed via the primary Nationality Law's structure (see ae_naturalisation.json), which conditions naturalisation on decades of residence under DIFFERENT visa categories, not specifically Golden Visa status, and via this dataset's general finding that residency (however prestigious) does not lead to citizenship in the UAE. The talent category's eligibility criteria are inherently qualitative/discretionary rather than numeric -- modelled with an enumerated category list rather than a single threshold, consistent with how the source itself describes it.
